ground.note: Page surface. Measured luminance 0.0036 against the dark-theme gate ceiling of 0.05.

plate.note: Figure/card/nav/footer/modal fill. Matches the source benchmark plots' canvas, so a real plot drops in unrestyled. Luminance 0.0061.

plate-2.note: Second-level surface: data-table stripes, current nav tab, topo wall face. Luminance 0.0106.

grid.note: The universal 1px boundary: every card border, strip divider, chart gridline, sample-point halo.

axis.note: Reserved for drawn axes and axis ticks, so an axis reads as structure and a gridline as reference.

ink.note: Body text, headings, readout values. 17.76:1 on ground.

ink-2.note: Plate labels, kickers, captions, deks, secondary metadata. 9.10:1 on ground.

ink-3.note: Footnotes, units, tick labels, off-route samples. 6.06:1 on plate and 5.60:1 on plate-2 — which is why footnotes never go below 14px.

series-1.note: DATA ONLY. Sampled from the committed benchmark plots. Draws the HNSW curve, its sample points, and the site mark's sample line — never an affordance.

series-2.note: EVERY INTERACTION. Sampled from the plots and darkened for contrast: 8.98:1 on ground. Links, focus ring, active-tab tick, primary fill, crosshair, callouts, timeline nodes, scroll trace. On a fill the label is always --ground; ink-on-amber is 1.98:1 and is never used.

series-3.note: The second measured series (IVF-PQ), plus the proof-chip status dot. Never used for emphasis.

logo-chip.note: The one true white: the chip behind employer logos, because vendor marks are drawn for paper. Nothing else on the dark theme is pure white. The @media print remap reuses raw paper values (#ffffff, #10161d, #0b3a6b, #8a5a00, #6b7885, #c4ccd4, #f2f4f7, #2f7d4f, #55606b) by design so no :root remap can regress the printed page.

display.purpose: The page h1 only. A clamp, so the name uses the width available at 1920/2560; held to 22ch so it breaks where it should.

headline.purpose: A page's lead section heading. Mobile floor sits above the rank-2 size so the two ranks never collapse on a phone, and never exceed the h1 above.

title.purpose: Supporting section headings and the contact band's heading.

body.purpose: Prose at 66ch; hero subhead and page deks at 56ch.

label.purpose: Kickers, provenance lines, chips, skills rails, callouts, plate labels. The 13px mono step is the same rank as an axis label.

footnote.purpose: Plate footnote strips, readout units, measurement conditions. 14px is a floor, not a default — ink-3 earns AA only at or above it.

shadows.name: hairline-halo
shadows.purpose: The halo around a sample point and a route hold. The only 'shadow' shape in the system.

shadows.name: current-tick
shadows.purpose: The amber tick under the current nav tab, set like an active tick under an axis.

shadows.name: finish-ring
shadows.purpose: The concentric ring on the topo's finish hold, the way a plot rings its annotated point.

motion.name: t-tap
motion.purpose: Button lift, border colour, crosshair transition, link colour.

motion.name: t-hover
motion.purpose: Card lift, timeline node scale, modal panel.

motion.name: t-reveal
motion.purpose: The scroll-reveal fade — the only load-time motion, gated on the .js root class AND prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing. No overshoot easing anywhere: this system highlights samples, it does not squash toys.

motion.name: keyframes
motion.purpose: The stylesheet declares no keyframes at all. One animated moment on the site (the user-driven crosshair); everything else is a transition on an interaction.

breakpoints.name: tiny
breakpoints.note: Nav brand hides; the tab row's left edge becomes the page's alignment anchor.

breakpoints.name: xs
breakpoints.note: Tab padding/gap tighten again to hold a >=12px right gutter.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.note: --section-gap drops to 48px; plate padding 16px; wordmark and box diagrams hide.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.note: --section-gap 64px; card grids go two-column at 768px; 44px title tap padding below.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.note: System plates and the About layout go two-column at 1024px.

figureNumbering.rule: Figure numbers belong to objects that genuinely are figures. Five FIG. labels are a system; nine are a costume.

print.strategy: Full token remap to paper, not a hidden stylesheet.
notes: Button print overrides use fixed values (#ffffff / #0b3a6b / #6b7885), not tokens, so no later :root remap can re-introduce the measured 1.59–1.86:1 cold-load collision.
The hero collapses to one column so the vacated figure column does not print blank.
Every revealable block is forced visible, because IntersectionObserver never fires when printing from a fresh load.
Injected chrome (progress rail, legend swatch, modal, drawn figures, box diagrams) is hidden.

gates.note: The gates are part of the design system: a visual rule that cannot survive them is not shipped.
items: scripts/check-facts.mjs — required/forbidden string gate, runs on every build. Axis labels are decimals and curve coordinates are literal d="…" attributes because of it.

verify.mjs — dark-surface luminance ceiling (0.05), caption/figure non-overlap at all three viewports, primary-CTA contrast >=4.5:1 at rest AND hovered, both prefers-reduced-motion queries present in the built CSS, frozen nav height and progress-rail geometry.
A separate private confidentiality scan runs before anything is pushed.

narrative.overview:
The site is set like a figure in a benchmark report, not like a portfolio. Every claim appears inside a plate that names itself, states its measurement conditions, and carries its limits as a footnote under a hairline. The palette was sampled from the benchmark plots committed in the featured repositories (amber darkened for contrast), so the world is not a theme applied to the work — it is the work's own drawing conventions promoted to page furniture. Density is high but never crowded: content sits on hairlines rather than in boxes-within-boxes, and separation is always a 1px rule.

The register is austere and instrumental. Surfaces are three near-black tones apart by a few points of luminance; type carries the hierarchy; saturated colour is rationed to two jobs and nothing else. Restraint here is a load-bearing claim — a page that spends its loudest colour on an intro course list is asserting that the course list is the evidence. The named failure mode of this world is reading unfinished rather than restrained: any gap, orphan, or unaligned edge is a bug in the spacing or type system, not a taste debate.

The confirmed rejection is the decorated-résumé default: a hero of name plus mono eyebrow plus serif aphorism plus four buttons over a decorative canvas, with the proof pushed below the fold. There is no aphorism slot, no decorative wallpaper, and no symmetric stat grid — metric counts vary (3 / 2 / 2) because a fixed count reads as a schema filled in rather than a measurement taken.
keyCharacteristics: Three near-black surfaces (ground / plate / plate-2), two hairline greys, a three-step ink ramp, three series colours.
Blue is data and lives only inside figures; amber is every interaction and every human annotation.
Seven primitives borrowed wholesale from plots: plate, axis rule, readout, sample point, callout, data table, label button.
One shadow in the system, and it is a hairline.
One animated moment, and it is user-driven.
Figure numbers only on objects that are genuinely figures.

rules.name: The Blue-Is-Data, Amber-Is-Interaction Rule
rules.body: --series-1 may appear only inside a figure, where the source plots already put it. Everything a reader can click, focus, or scrub is --series-2. No third meaning for either colour, ever.

rules.name: The Ground-On-Amber Rule
rules.body: An amber fill takes a --ground label. There is no exception and no lighter amber that changes this; the 1.98:1 alternative is a measured invisible-CTA defect that the build carries a gate against.

rules.name: The Two-Jobs Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour is spent on evidence and on affordances. Content that is metadata — coursework, skills, tech tags — is set in --ink-2 / --ink-3 on a hairline, never coloured to look important.

rules.name: The Fourteen-Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing set in --ink-3 goes below 14px. Tick labels at 11px and plate labels at 12px are set in --ink-2 or brighter.

rules.name: The Rank Rule
rules.body: A section declares its rank and the heading size moves with the gap above it. Five identically-sized headings over five identical pads is the generated-page fingerprint; rank-1 opens a page, everything supporting it is rank-2.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any element that shows a measured number carries the mono family and font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Numbers in this world line up.

rules.name: The Hairline-Only Rule
rules.body: The only shadow in this system is a hairline. If a box-shadow has a blur radius or an alpha, it does not belong here.

rules.name: The Border-Not-Blur Rule
rules.body: State is signalled by the boundary going amber plus a 1px translate, at most. Cards move 2px, buttons 1px, and pressing removes the lift entirely.

dos: Do keep --series-1 inside figures and make every clickable, focusable, or scrubbable thing --series-2.
Do put a --ground label on any amber fill.
Do wrap a measured claim in a plate, with its conditions and its limits in the footnote strip.

Do number a figure only when the object genuinely is one. The build ships five: FIG. 00 (boulder topo), FIG. 01 (the Sweep), FIG. 02–04 (the three system plates), plus FIG. 404 on the not-found page. About, Education, and Skills get typographic rank instead — five FIG. labels are a system, nine are a costume.
Do vary the number of readout rows with the evidence (3 / 2 / 2 as shipped).
Do state a section's rank so the heading size and the gap above it move together.
Do use --section-gap for section separation and the 4→96px ladder for everything else.
Do set every measured number in mono with tabular figures, and keep footnotes at 14px or larger.
Do write a hover state once, at one specificity, with the label colour restated from the variant's own custom property.
Do keep proof in the markup. If it only exists after a pointermove, a hover, a scroll, or a bundle load, it is not proof.
Do remap the palette to paper under @media print, with fixed-value overrides on the button primitive so no later :root remap can re-introduce a low-contrast collision.
Do let a figure pan on narrow screens rather than shrinking its labels below legibility, and start the pan at the annotated end.

Do treat the build gates as part of the design system: the fact gate, and verify.mjs's dark-surface luminance ceiling, caption/figure non-overlap assertion, and primary-CTA contrast assertion at rest and hovered.
donts: Don't give --series-1 an interactive role, or give amber a data role.
Don't put --ink on an amber fill (1.98:1).
Don't add a blurred or alpha box-shadow. The only shadow is a hairline; the three existing box-shadow uses are hairline halos, rings, and the active-tab tick.
Don't use a gradient to fill a surface. Gradients here generate evenly spaced hairline ticks and nothing else.
Don't introduce a second radius. 2px for everything rectangular, the pill only for non-interactive chips and the timeline group label.
Don't add a second :hover rule for the label button, and don't qualify one with :not() — that is the exact shape of the invisible-CTA defect this system was rebuilt around.
Don't add an entrance animation or a keyframe. The stylesheet declares no keyframes at all; the site is entitled to one animated moment and the crosshair has it.
Don't let anything revealable start hidden under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, and don't place a revealable element inside a display:none container.
Don't put a figure number on About, Education, Skills, or the contact band.
Don't build a fixed-column metric grid to hold varying evidence.
Don't colour metadata — coursework, skills, tech tags — to compete with evidence.
Don't set padding shorthand on .hero, .page-head, or .not-found: they share their element with .container, and a shorthand zeroes the page's horizontal gutter.
Don't change the nav's 64px height or the progress rail's box, and don't un-hide the brand below 360px — the tab row's left edge is an alignment anchor there.
